# fshy: every record in full

> A catalogue of free, nearly free and cheapest-paid cloud capacity: storage, compute and GPU time, model inference, egress and tunnels, proxies, crawling, debrid, netdisks, databases, email, DNS and domains, CI runners, developer services, data APIs and coding subscriptions. 4,866 records from 3,445 providers. Each record states its quota, the limit that runs out first, the identity a signup costs (email, phone, card, ID), its evidence and how fresh that evidence is.

Data as of 2026-11-10, the date of the published data. Version `e7cf1b4a40af`: the first 12 hex digits of the SHA-256 of every record's Markdown, topic by topic in the one order (hosted before self-hosted, then verdict, provider name, record id); it changes whenever a record does.

All 4,866 records are 21,438 KB, about 5,794K tokens in Markdown, more than any context window holds, so the text is split: one file per topic when the topic fits in 300 KB, about 81K tokens, else one per verdict group with the topic's self-hosted records in one last group, and a group over that size into balanced parts. Every record is in exactly one part. The parts below come topic by topic, each topic in the one order (hosted before self-hosted, then verdict, provider name, record id), and every self-hosted part comes after all of them, in the last group, 'Self-hosted, the last resort'; a topic in one file holds its self-hosted records at its end. To answer a question, read the topic's one-line index, https://fshy.ajam.dev/t/<topic>.md, then the provider pages it links, https://fshy.ajam.dev/p/<id>.md; or query the store.

## How to read a record

Each record opens with its id (topic/slug), verdict, evidence, binding limit and category. Then it says what a signup needs, when the record was verified and when that check goes stale. Then it gives its URL and its provider page. Each line of the lists below is one term and its meaning.

- verdict, best first:
  - `qualifies`: usable as stated; the read path was probed
  - `qualifies-with-caveat`: usable, with a named limit or an unprobed read path
  - `trial-only`: a time-boxed or one-time trial, not a recurring allowance
  - `paid-only`: no free allowance; listed for its price
  - `fails-identity`: the identity required is not reachable without it
  - `fails-egress`: data cannot be read back out at a usable rate or price
  - `fails-quota`: the free allowance is too small to matter
  - `dead`: the offer or the service no longer exists
- group, the verdicts that a topic page lists together:
  - `usable`: verdict qualifies or qualifies-with-caveat
  - `trial`: verdict trial-only
  - `paid`: verdict paid-only
  - `rejected`: verdict fails-identity, fails-egress or fails-quota
  - `dead`: verdict dead
- evidence, how a claim is backed, strongest first:
  - `measured`: a live request was made and its output kept
  - `documented`: a first-party page was read and the sentence quoted
  - `reported`: a third party said so
  - `inferred`: reasoned from other evidence
  - `unverified`: asserted and not checked
- binding, the limit that runs out first:
  - `request-rate`: requests per unit of time
  - `pull-count`: number of downloads or pulls
  - `per-ip-shaping`: bandwidth shaped per address or port
  - `per-object-cap`: largest single object
  - `write-gated`: writes need approval, payment or a gate
  - `retention-clamped`: data is deleted after a period
  - `volume-quota`: total stored or transferred volume
  - `none`: no named constraint binds
- identity, what a signup costs:
  - `anonymous`: nothing is asked for
  - `email`: an email address
  - `any-phone`: a phone number from any country
  - `country-phone`: a phone number from a named country
  - `national-id`: a government identity document
  - `card`: a payment card
  - `institution`: membership of a university, lab or company
- `needs card, phone, ID, institution`: yes, no or unknown. Unknown never means no. In an index, `?` after the identity marks a placeholder that no source states, and `card?` or `phone?` an unknown requirement.
- `free tier` or `no free tier` in an index: the record states a free allowance, or states that it has none. Neither word: the record does not say.
- verified: when the record was last verified, with `checked` after it when the check date of the staleness policy differs; then the basis:
  - `live`: the record was checked against the service
  - `inherited`: carried from an earlier source; checked_on is an upper bound
- stale on: the date that the evidence window of the check ends. Compare it with today. An index line says `stale since` in place of `stale on` when that date is on or before the date of the data.
- price: the price as written, then `parsed` USD figures where a number parsed. No parsed figure means none parsed, not free.
- `[n]`: a numbered source; the sources list of the record gives each URL once. An evidence line reads: source, date, what it proved.
- `self-hosted, last resort`: in place of the verdict, software or a node that the user installs, runs and maintains; the verdict follows it as `verdict <word>`. Every list puts it after every hosted record. Self-hosted options are listed last, because this site is for users who have no hardware.
- not stated, not recorded, not applicable: the value was not published, or does not apply. A field that a record does not show was not published: that is unknown, not absent.
- the same as: the value equals an earlier line of the record, word for word.
- part of: the value is a part of an earlier line of the record. That line holds it in full.

### Self-hosted, the last resort

Software or a node that the user installs, runs and maintains. Self-hosted options are listed last, because this site is for users who have no hardware.

- [Storage: Self-hosted, the last resort](https://fshy.ajam.dev/t/storage/llms-full-self-hosted.txt): 70 records; 186 KB, about 50K tokens
- [Compute: Self-hosted, the last resort](https://fshy.ajam.dev/t/compute/llms-full-self-hosted.txt): 34 records; 104 KB, about 28K tokens

- [Developer services: Self-hosted, the last resort](https://fshy.ajam.dev/t/dev-services/llms-full-self-hosted.txt): 4 records; 57 KB, about 15K tokens

## Query it

- [MCP endpoint](https://fshy.ajam.dev/about/#api): POST JSON-RPC 2.0 to `https://fshy.ajam.dev/mcp` (Streamable HTTP; a GET there answers 405), stateless and read-only; tools help, search, filter, get, entity, need, sql, worklist. Connect: `claude mcp add --transport http fshy https://fshy.ajam.dev/mcp`
- [help.txt](https://fshy.ajam.dev/api/v1/help.txt): the query primer: tables, columns, vocabularies and worked SQL; read it first
- [search](https://fshy.ajam.dev/api/v1/search?q=gpu+hours&topic=compute): full-text search; `q` words, optional `topic`
- [records](https://fshy.ajam.dev/api/v1/records?topic=storage&no_card=1&sort=usd_per_tb_month): filter and sort record cards; `free=1` keeps the records with a free allowance
- [sql](https://fshy.ajam.dev/api/v1/sql?q=SELECT+rid,verdict+FROM+record+LIMIT+5): read-only SQLite over the store
- [record](https://fshy.ajam.dev/api/v1/record/compute/oracle-cloud): one record as JSON, `/api/v1/record/<topic>/<slug>`
- [entity](https://fshy.ajam.dev/api/v1/entity/oracle.json): one provider and all its records as JSON, `/api/v1/entity/<id>.json`
- [schema.sql](https://fshy.ajam.dev/api/v1/schema.sql): the store's schema; [vocab.json](https://fshy.ajam.dev/api/v1/vocab.json): its vocabularies
- [fshy-public.sqlite.gz](https://fshy.ajam.dev/data/fshy-public.sqlite.gz): the whole store as one SQLite file, gzip. data/manifest.json gives public_db.gzip_sha256, the SHA-256 of this download, and public_db.sha256, the SHA-256 of the SQLite file after gunzip
